question.text: In a screw gauge, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> complete rotations of the screw cause it to move a linear distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. There are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn></math> circular scale divisions. The thickness of a wire measured by this screw gauge gives a reading of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn></math> main scale divisions and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn></math> circular scale divisions. Assuming negligible zero error, what is the thickness (in mm) of the wire?
